next_investigations: Compare vibration and alarm rates by sensor to determine whether the S04–S06 cluster drives the overall correlation, or whether other sensors also show the relationship.
Analyze vibration and alarm trends over time (by week or by month) to identify whether the patterns are stable, seasonal, or deteriorating across the 3-month period.

Examine the 264 alarm events in detail: their timing, which sensors and lines they occur on, and the vibration levels at the moment each alarm fires, to test whether a vibration threshold can predict alarms.
methodology_concerns: Temperature and Vibration readings are averaged, not time-weighted, so they do not reflect the actual time each condition persisted; a brief spike counts the same as a sustained elevation.

Sensors S04, S05, and S06 average vibration readings of 3.15, 3.21, and 3.19 mm/s respectively, while the remaining five sensors all average between 1.97 and 2.01 mm/s.
High vibration causes the alarms, so damping the line B sensors will stop them.
